title: PSVR-C — project continuity vs a strong native baseline on two interdependent project workloads
statusNote: The owner authorized the cohort on 2026-11-05 ('均授权'). This stage runs the SOFTWARE scenario only; the cross-domain scenario is a separate stage that needs its own authorization.

hypotheses.statement: On an interrupted multi-artifact project, project continuity reduces repeated investigation and re-implementation of work that already exists.
hypotheses.null: The F baseline re-investigates and re-writes the same amount as A after the interruption.
observable: files read again after the interruption that the agent had already read before it
lines rewritten that survive to the final result
tokens spent between the new session start and the first result-producing action

hypotheses.statement: When a new fact invalidates part of the work, result continuation preserves the still-valid part instead of restarting the artifact.
hypotheses.null: The revised artifact differs from a from-scratch rewrite by no less than the preserved work.
observable: artifact lines that predate the new fact and remain in the accepted result
the count of downstream artifacts revised only where the fact requires it
the checker's pass/fail on the accepted head

hypotheses.statement: On-demand governance (A) costs less than default governed execution (G) for the same usable outcome.
hypotheses.null: A and G have the same total tokens per usable outcome.
hypotheses.note: G is diagnostic only and is not required in every cohort.

hypotheses.statement: In tasks with asynchronous cross-artifact dependencies, the governed path reduces wrong acceptance or mutually inconsistent artifacts.
hypotheses.null: F and A produce the same number of source-inconsistent artifacts.
observable: the scenario checker's assertions on the accepted head
operator findings that name an inconsistency the checker did not

F.definition: F+Finish+Commit: native DSH with native tools, subagents, worktrees and Git; ONE explicit instruction to stop when the deliverable is complete and to commit it. No Palimpsest project, Work, World, relay or episode.

A.definition: The adaptive product path: the principal starts from the user goal and decides whether to work directly, use a native subagent, delegate formal Work, continue an interrupted attempt, finalize and conclude. No fixed agent count and no pre-declared task graph in the prompt.

G.definition: Diagnostic only: the full governed Work path with a declared plan, used to separate the cost of complete governance from adaptation.

the REST baseline tests still pass

scenarios.deliverable: six interdependent deployment artifacts with a consistent recommendation
acceptance: node check.mjs --final exits 0 on the accepted head
the cost arithmetic and the schedule dates are re-derived from the sources

interruptionControls.MATCHED_TOKEN: session 1 is stopped at 400,000 reported tokens in both conditions
interruptionControls.MATCHED_WORK_STATE: session 1 is stopped after the first valid commit of the migration work (the token milestone is the primary control; the work-state control is recorded from the snapshot)

interruptionControls.MATCHED_TOKEN: session 1 is stopped at 400,000 reported tokens in both conditions
interruptionControls.MATCHED_WORK_STATE: session 1 is stopped after the first valid commit of package work (the token milestone is the primary control; the snapshot records the work state)

measurement.business: does the accepted head pass the scenario's own executable check
measurement.durability: is the deliverable committed, and can it be rebuilt from the accepted commit alone
measurement.governance: was the result accepted by the operator through the product's own path
measurement.autonomy: did the agent choose collaboration, replanning and the end of the episode itself
measurement.cost: total reported tokens, tool calls, wall time, and cost per usable outcome

controls.no_oracle: no evaluator oracle, no correct task graph and no final solution in any prompt
controls.no_post_hoc_repair: a prompt is not repaired after the run starts
controls.labelled_standins: a deterministic stand-in is labelled and never scored as a cognitive agent
controls.scoring: business scoring is a separate pass over the accepted head; it is not read by the running agent
